title: Invite teammates by email link
summary: Workspace admins can invite people by email. The invitee gets a single-use link, signs in or signs up, and lands in the workspace with the role the admin chose. Today admins create accounts by hand and share passwords over chat.

tabs.title: Overview
tabs.problem: Adding a teammate means an admin creates the account, picks a temporary password, and sends it over Slack. Support sees about a dozen *"I can't log in"* tickets a week from this, and passwords sit in chat history indefinitely.
tabs.change: Admins enter an email and a role. The invitee receives a link that is valid once and for seven days. Following it signs them in (or up) and creates their membership.

goals.title: No shared passwords
goals.detail: Nobody but the invitee ever knows their credentials.

goals.title: Role chosen up front
goals.detail: The membership is created with the role the admin picked, so there is no second step to fix permissions.

goals.title: Admins can see and revoke pending invites
goals.detail: A pending invitation is visible on the members page until it is accepted, revoked or expired.

out_of_scope: Inviting someone to more than one workspace at once
Changing the email address on a pending invite (revoke and re-invite instead)

findings.note: Memberships already carry a `role` enum and a unique index on `(workspace_id, user_id)`; the invite flow should create through `Memberships::Create` rather than inserting directly.
Authorization is a Pundit policy per model. `WorkspacePolicy#manage_members?` is the check the members page uses today.

steps.label: Authorize manage_members? and check seat limit
Enqueue invite email with raw token

flows.trigger: The invitee opens the link from the email.

entities.name: Invitation
entities.definition: A single-use offer of a role in one workspace, addressed to one email.
rules: Created only by a member who passes `manage_members?`
Pending until accepted, revoked or past `expires_at` (7 days)
Accepting it requires the signed-in user's verified email to match
constraints: At most one pending invitation per `(workspace_id, email)`
Token digest is unique; the raw token is never stored
Accepted, revoked and expired are terminal

entities.name: Membership
entities.definition: Existing model. Gains no columns; invites create one through `Memberships::Create`.
rules: Role comes from the invitation, never from the accept request

blocks.caption: New table: invitations
rows: Unique; SHA-256 of the raw token

blocks.title: A partial unique index enforces one pending invite per email
blocks.body: `UNIQUE (workspace_id, email) WHERE accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`. Expired rows still count until a nightly job revokes them, which keeps the index simple.

cases.title: Link accepted twice at the same moment
cases.detail: Two tabs or a double click race the accept. Without a row lock both create a membership and one fails on the unique index with a 500. Lock the invitation row and treat an already-accepted invitation for the same user as success.

cases.title: Invitee signs in with a different email
cases.detail: Someone forwards the link and the recipient signs in with their own account. Accepting would grant access to whoever holds the link. Refuse and explain which address the invite was for.

cases.title: Seat limit reached between invite and accept
cases.detail: The limit was checked at send time but other invites were accepted since. Re-check at accept and show the invitee a clear *ask your admin* page instead of a generic error.

cases.title: Inviting someone who is already a member
cases.detail: The admin does not realise they are already in. Return a validation error naming the existing role rather than sending a pointless email.

cases.title: Inviter loses admin rights before acceptance
cases.detail: The invitation still reflects a decision the workspace made. Keep it valid, but show revoked-by-owner as the only way to cancel it.

risks.title: Invitation link as a bearer credential
risks.exposure: Anyone who obtains the link could join the workspace with the invited role, including admin.
mitigations: Require the signed-in user's verified email to match the invitation
Single use, 7-day expiry, and revocable from the members page
Store only the SHA-256 of the token so a database leak yields no usable links

risks.title: Email enumeration through the invite form
risks.exposure: The *already a member* error reveals whether an address belongs to the workspace. Only admins can reach the form, so the exposure is to insiders.

risks.title: Invite spam
risks.exposure: A compromised admin account could send many invitations from our domain.
mitigations: Cap pending invitations at 50 per workspace
Rate-limit to 20 per hour per inviter

gaps.title: SSO-only workspaces
gaps.detail: I have not checked how workspaces that enforce SAML handle a sign-up from an invite link. That needs a decision from whoever owns SSO before slice planning.

gaps.title: Email deliverability
gaps.detail: Bounces are not surfaced to the admin. The mailer supports bounce webhooks, but wiring them is a separate piece of work.
